result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as mock resources. I haven't run the specific cases from your description (`mock/`, `mock.data`, `mock-größe`, `remock/`, `mock.java` and the rest). The existing `Scoping*` tests in `codeanalyzer` pass.

In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394), I changed the two rules from `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` to `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`.

- **Plain `mock/`:** the old rules needed at least one character after `mock`, so the folder name alone never matched.
- **Punctuation and non-ASCII names:** `[^/]*` accepts any characters after `mock`, including `.`, `(` and `ö`.
- **Staying in one folder name:** the leading `/` and the closing `/` keep the match inside a single folder. `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` don't match.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already also tries each path with backslashes converted to `/`, so Windows-style paths are covered without further changes.
- **Previously matched folders:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still match, since `[^/]*` covers everything the old class did.

As before, the rule needs a `/` before the folder name, so a `mock/` folder at the very start of a relative path with no parent still isn't caught.
